chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, he raised it (to the Imam), saying:
The Penalty (Hadd) during travel is for the one who commits adultery; he is not stoned even if he is married (Muhsan), (i.e., a journey where he) shortens (the Prayer) and breaks the Fast.

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for a married person committing adultery while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that the penalty of Rajm (stoning) for a Muhsan (married person) is suspended during travel because the prerequisite of maintaining full religious obligations—specifically continuous prayer and fasting—is disrupted by the concessions of Safar. Shia jurists interpret this as a link between the severity of the Hadd penalty and the completeness of the individual's spiritual state, noting that the temporary relaxation of duties during travel mitigates the full weight of the punishment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn,

(It has been narrated) that he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘The Penalty (Hadd) during the travel for the one who commits adultery, he would not be stoned even if he was married, (a journey where he has to) shorten (the Prayer) and break the Fast’.
